The Friendliest Cat Breeds for Families

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 10:12
Instaread

Cats make a wonderful addition to a family, bringing joy, companionship and a bit of playful chaos. When searching for the cat breed that’s right for you, it’s important to consider your unique family situation. Do you have small children? Are you an experienced pet parent or first-time cat owner? How much maintenance — like daily grooming — are you willing to do? All of these factors can influence your choice.

To assist you in choosing the right cat for your family, we have gathered information about some of the cat breeds that are known to be great family pets. Keep in mind that there are many other breeds, as well as mixed breeds, that can also be very friendly and make wonderful family cats. This is not an exhaustive list but rather a starting point for your selection.

The Best House Cat Breeds

The best cat breeds for indoor-only living are those that combine an affectionate temperament with adaptability to smaller spaces. These breeds are friendly, enjoy human interaction and thrive in indoor settings.

American Shorthair

American shorthairs are known for their friendly personalities, sweet nature and playful curiosity. They will entertain themselves with toys but are also happy to spend time and interact with their family. They do well in homes with kids and other cats. However, they have a strong hunting instinct that may take over with birds or smaller pets in the home.

American shorthair cats typically weigh between 6 and 15 pounds and live 15 to 20 years. They have a short, dense coat that requires minimal maintenance, so a weekly brushing is usually sufficient.

Persian

One of the oldest and most popular cat breeds, Persian cats are admired for their long, flowing coats, round faces and large, expressive eyes. They have a gentle nature and are calm and affectionate, preferring a quiet environment where they can relax and spend time with their family. While they enjoy companionship, Persians are generally less active than many other breeds and are content lounging in comfortable spots around the home.

These medium- to large-sized cats typically weigh between 7 and 12 pounds and have an average lifespan of 12 to 17 years. The luxurious coat of a Persian cat requires daily brushing to prevent tangles and mats, and their flat facial structure means regular eye cleaning may also be needed to keep them healthy and comfortable.

The Best Cat Breeds for Kids

Before bringing a cat home, it’s essential to teach children how to care for and interact safely with them. Teaching your children to respect a cat’s boundaries will help build a lasting, positive bond. Here are some of the best cat breeds for families with young children.

British Shorthair

The British shorthair cat has a short, dense coat and a distinctive rounded head and face, which resembles that of a teddy bear. They are loving, patient, easy-going and affectionate, but they are not demanding or clingy. With a calm demeanor, British shorthairs get along well with respectful and gentle children. However, they prefer to seek attention on their own terms, favoring quiet and peaceful interactions.

British shorthairs typically have a medium to large build, featuring round faces, chubby cheeks and large round eyes that can be copper, gold or blue. Their dense and plush fur requires regular grooming, usually at least once a week to prevent matting and to remove loose hair.

Birman

Birman cats are a gentle, affectionate breed known for being loyal companions. They are easy to handle and are great for families with children and most dogs. While quieter than some breeds, they enjoy playtime and can often be found fetching balls or playing with interactive toys.

These medium- to large-sized cats typically weigh around 12 pounds and have an average lifespan of 9 to 15 years. Birmans are known for their stunning, semi-longhaired coat and striking, sapphire blue eyes. They have white gloves on all four feet and white markings that lace up the back of their hind legs, creating a striking contrast with their main coat color. Birmans have what is called a “single coat,” meaning they do not have an undercoat and are easy to groom.

The Most Affectionate Cat Breeds

If you’re searching for a loving feline companion, here are some breeds known for their people-oriented personalities.

Sphynx

The sphynx cat is famous for its hairless coat and large ears, but these social butterflies also love to attract attention. This medium-sized breed is sleek and muscular, typically weighing under 12 pounds. Sphynx cats are friendly, loving and loyal — often following their owners around the house to be involved in daily activities. They are known as an affectionate cat breed, so be prepared for them to seize any opportunity to perch on your shoulder or curl up in your lap.

While the sphynx cat may seem completely bald at first glance, they actually have a fine, short coat of fuzz that gives their skin a texture similar to suede. Because they lack normal fur to absorb body oils, they require regular grooming to manage their skin. They usually need baths every 1 to 3 weeks with a gentle, hypoallergenic shampoo to prevent oil buildup.

Burmese

Burmese cats are an excellent choice if you are looking for an exceptionally affectionate companion. They are playful and love being around people to the point that they are often called “Velcro cats.” With their remarkable golden eyes and innocent expression, Burmese cats thrive on attention. For cat lovers who want a pet experience that feels highly interactive and engaging, Burmese cats can be a great match. However, because they crave this close human contact, this breed might not be the best fit for you if you’re often away from home.

Burmese cats come in various colors, including champagne, blue, fawn and platinum, although most are deep sable brown. They are medium-sized cats with a substantial bone structure, which makes them appear more muscular and sometimes heavier than they actually are —  averaging between 9 and 13 pounds. They have short, fine coats that lie close to their body, featuring a satin-like finish. Their grooming needs are minimal, making them low-maintenance pets.

Himalayan

A mix of Persian and Siamese breeds, these cats are known for their long, luxurious coats, flat faces and striking blue eyes. They are friendly and sociable, getting along well with just about everyone. They also have a playful, kitten-like side and enjoy interaction with their human family members.

Himalayans are medium-sized cats that typically weigh between 7 and 12 pounds and have an average lifespan of 9 to 15 years. It’s important to note that they require a high-maintenance grooming routine — they need to be brushed every day to prevent their long hair from matting. Himalayans are prone to some hereditary health issues, including brachycephalic airway syndrome, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and polycystic kidney disease.

Family-Friendly Cat Breeds

These cat breeds are known for being affectionate, patient and social, making them excellent companions for families with children and other pets.

Ragdoll

They are one of the larger cat breeds, known for their calm and affectionate nature, as well as their gentle temperament. They are exceptionally friendly and are well suited to households with children, other cats and other animals. Ragdoll cats enjoy spending time with their people, often following them from room to room. While they have an easygoing nature, they also enjoy interactive play with feather wands, balls and puzzle toys that engage their curious minds.

These large, sturdy cats typically weigh between 10 and 20 pounds, and have an average lifespan of 12 to 17 years. They are best known for their luxurious, semi-longhaired coat, brilliant blue eyes and color-point markings. Their silky, plush coat comes in a variety of patterns and colors, including seal, blue, chocolate, lilac, flame and cream. They are not talkative cats, but may greet you with a soft mew from time to time.

Maine Coon

Often called “gentle giants,” these are one of the largest domestic cat breeds. They are highly affectionate, patient with children and love participating in household activities. One unique aspect of Maine coons is their intelligence. They are highly trainable and can learn to respond to commands and even play fetch. They are curious, outgoing and adventurous, so be prepared; they love to explore their surroundings.

These large, muscular cats typically weigh between 10 and 25 pounds, and they have an average lifespan of 10 to 15 years. Maine coons have a long, shaggy, water-resistant coat that comes in a wide variety of colors and patterns. Their tufted ears, bushy tails and expressive eyes give them a distinctive appearance. Regular brushing helps keep their thick coat healthy and free of tangles, especially during seasonal shedding.

Siamese

The Siamese cat is a historic breed that was first introduced to the United States as a gift to President Rutherford B. Hayes. Known for their intelligence, Siamese cats can even be trained to walk on a leash! They thrive on close companionship with their owners, and are happy to climb into your lap seeking both attention and warmth. Their striking bright blue eyes and fine, short coats featuring darker pigment on their faces, ears, paws and tails make them a beautiful breed.

Siamese cats are extremely social and form strong bonds with their families. They are quite vocal and often express themselves with loud meows, especially when it’s mealtime or when they want more attention. They have a relatively long lifespan, averaging between 15 and 20 years. However, it’s important to note that these intelligent slender cats have a few quirks; they dislike being left alone for long periods and may become destructive or mischievous when they are bored.

 

Adding a cat or kitten to your family is an important decision. It requires careful consideration of which cat is best suited to your family’s lifestyle, as well as matching the cat’s personality to your household dynamics. By taking these factors into account, you can make an informed choice and find a feline friend that will be a beloved member of your family for many years to come.

The information in this blog has been developed with a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine and is designed to help educate pet parents. If you have questions or concerns about your pet's health or nutrition, please talk with your veterinarian.
